# claude-terrarium: everything in one file

> Mods for Claude Code from the marketplace Guhan-SenSam/claude-terrarium. Four mods, each installed alone: thinking-weather, system-monitor, turn-receipt, pins. Source: https://github.com/Guhan-SenSam/claude-terrarium. Docs: https://guhan-sensam.github.io/claude-terrarium/

## Facts

- Mods are Claude Code plugins with function hooks (TypeScript hooks modules). Built and tested on Claude Code 2.1.325.
- Marketplace source: `Guhan-SenSam/claude-terrarium`. Once added it is named `claude-terrarium`, so plugin ids are `<mod>@claude-terrarium`.
- Visual parts (thinking-weather's background and working row, system-monitor's pixel band) draw in the Claude Code desktop app. The terminal shows text parts only.
- system-monitor reads Linux `/proc` (and `nvidia-smi` when present).
- Nothing leaves the machine except thinking-weather's real weather, which is off until a town is set.
- The mods make no sound.

## Install

    claude plugin install <mod> --marketplace Guhan-SenSam/claude-terrarium --scope user

Mods: thinking-weather, system-monitor, turn-receipt, pins. Check with `claude plugin list` (each shows `<mod>@claude-terrarium`, enabled). Mods load at session start: restart the session or run `/reload-plugins`.

Desktop app, by hand: + next to the prompt box, Plugins, Add marketplace `Guhan-SenSam/claude-terrarium`, Add plugin.
Terminal prompt: `/plugin install <mod> --marketplace Guhan-SenSam/claude-terrarium`.

Update: `claude plugin update <mod>@claude-terrarium`, then restart or `/reload-plugins`.
Uninstall: `claude plugin uninstall <mod>@claude-terrarium`.

## thinking-weather

A pixel-art valley (320x180 vector pixel art) behind the conversation in the desktop app.

What it shows:

| When | The valley |
|---|---|
| Claude idle | A clear sky, or the set town's real weather |
| Claude working | Storm clouds glide in from the corners and top; rain once they arrive; the bottom working row becomes a pixel storm cloud |
| Each tool call or slash command | A lightning strike |
| A failed tool call | A red strike |
| Waiting on the person (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode) | Rain stops, the lantern blinks |
| Turn finished | Clouds roll out, sunbeams |
| A subagent at work | Something flying at the side of the sky until it finishes: a leaf kite, a diamond kite, a hot-air balloon, a drone or a hover probe, by era |
| `git commit` or `git push` | A firework |
| Compaction | Fog rolls through |
| A long turn | Heavier rain after 2 minutes, darker after 5 |

Eras follow the context window: 0-20% Stone Age, 20-40% village, 40-60% industrial (a mill with stacks, a steam train, brick terraces, coal smoke), 60-80% modern (turbines, pylons, flats and glass towers), 80-100% sci-fi (spires, space elevator, hovercraft, ringed planet, aurora at night, an ion storm in place of the rain clouds). Compaction rolls fog in and resets society to the Stone Age.

Messages (desktop and mobile): the chat column is not blurred; each message sits in a see-through box framed for the era (stone: thick flint brown; village: thin parchment gold; industrial: double brass; modern: rounded steel blue; sci-fi: rounded neon cyan). The person's messages have a stronger fill than Claude's. Frames follow era previews; the terminal is unchanged.

The outside world: the sky follows the local clock (dawn, day, dusk, night, sun and moon); with a town set, dawn and dusk land on its real sunrise and sunset and the moon shows its real phase. Seasons by date (southern hemisphere flipped): spring blossom, summer wheat, autumn trees, a muted winter; snow on the ground only when the weather reports snow (with no town, winter is snowy). With a town set, the idle sky follows its weather: clear, partly, overcast, rain, snow, fog, thunder. Holidays: Halloween (from Oct 15), December, New Year's Eve, July 4.

Commands (all one command, /terrarium-weather, then what to change; bare, it says what shows):

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| /terrarium-weather place <town> | Follow a town's real weather ("Town, Region" disambiguates); `off` stops |
| /terrarium-weather era <era> | Preview stone, village, industrial, modern, scifi; `auto`; bare: say where society stands |
| /terrarium-weather sky <sky> | Preview clear, partly, overcast, rain, snow, fog, thunder; `auto` |
| /terrarium-weather season <season> | Preview spring, summer, autumn, winter, snow; `auto` |
| /terrarium-weather holiday <name> | Preview halloween, christmas, newyear, july4; `none`, `auto`; bare: say what shows |
| /terrarium-weather time HH:MM | Sky at a time of day; `auto` |
| /terrarium-weather reset | Clear every preview (sky, season, era, holiday, time) |
| /terrarium-weather cycle [seconds] | A whole day sped up (default 48 s) |
| /terrarium-weather tour | 40-second slideshow of seasons and skies |
| /terrarium-weather demo | Kites, a firework, a red strike, fog |
| /terrarium-weather now | What shows and why |
| /terrarium-weather test | A burst of test lightning |
| /terrarium-weather off | Clear the background for this session |

Tools it gives Claude:

| Tool | Input | Use |
|---|---|---|
| mcp__thinking-weather__weather_preview | sky, season, holiday, era (a name or "auto"), hour (0-24) | Show a look in clear weather; "auto" returns |
| mcp__thinking-weather__weather_place | town, or "off" | Set or clear the real-weather town |
| mcp__thinking-weather__weather_cycle | seconds (10-600) | Play a day sped up |

Setting `place` (string, default empty). Ask the person before setting it: the town's name is sent to Open-Meteo once, then coordinates rounded to about 10 km every 30 minutes.

    echo '{"place":"Tampa, Florida"}' | claude plugin configure thinking-weather@claude-terrarium --values-stdin

Stored in ~/.claude/settings.json as `"pluginConfigs": { "thinking-weather@claude-terrarium": { "options": { "place": "Tampa, Florida" } } }`. A copy loaded with --plugin-dir uses the key `thinking-weather@inline`.

Limits: draws in the desktop app only; the live tool-step row's orb is the app's own; no sound.

## system-monitor

A band above the prompt: pixel icons (chip, memory stick, graphics card), each with a bar of chunky segments and its reading. Green under 70%, gold from 70%, lantern orange from 90%, a glow brighter as it climbs; warmer at dawn and dusk, dimmer at night. A runtime-suspended GPU is left asleep (dimmed, "z"). Narrow prompts drop the bars, keeping icons and numbers. The terminal shows text bars like `CPU ████░░░░  42%`. `/terrarium-monitor` toggles a pane with threads, load average, memory, swap, VRAM and GPU temperature. Refreshes every 2 seconds; Linux only; NVIDIA optional.

## turn-receipt

A one-line receipt under each finished reply, e.g. `4m 12s · 23 tool calls · 2 agents · edited register.tsx, sample.ts +4 · 3.2k tokens out`. Interrupted turns read `interrupted after …`. Shown on desktop, terminal and phone; kept for the last 30 sessions.

## pins

Desktop: hover a reply and press Pin (Unpin to remove). Phone and terminal: `/terrarium-pins add` pins Claude's last reply. `/terrarium-pins` shows or hides the Pinned pane (newest first, with pin times). Kept for the last 30 sessions.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| No background | The terminal draws none; use the desktop app. Restart or /reload-plugins after install or update |
| "registered /<command> but no command.run hook answered it" | A copy of the mod was unloaded mid-session; restart |
| Two bands or competing backgrounds | An installed copy and a development copy are both loaded; remove the development copy |
| Sky stays clear with a town set | Run /terrarium-weather now; the settings key must be thinking-weather@claude-terrarium |
